claims.text: Enhanced-sampling molecular dynamics, such as replica exchange or umbrella sampling, can be used to study the thermal response of FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticles.
The thermal stability of FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticles increases with particle size.
Larger particles have larger free-energy barriers against thermally induced structural transitions.
The initial FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticles are nearly equiatomic solid solutions.
Enhanced-sampling MD can compute free-energy profiles and capture structural transitions over different nanoparticle sizes and temperatures.
The simulations will cover temperatures from near ambient to high application-relevant temperatures and multiple nanoparticle sizes.
Thermal evolution can involve surface or internal structural transitions such as phase separation or surface reconstruction.
Replica exchange or umbrella sampling efficiently overcomes kinetic barriers and allows access to rare thermally induced transitions.
Increasing nanoparticle size increases structural constraints and atomic coordination.
The increased structural constraints and coordination in larger particles produce higher free-energy barriers.
Higher free-energy barriers delay or suppress thermally induced structural transitions.
Larger FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticles will exhibit improved thermal stability relative to smaller particles under similar conditions.
Standard MD without enhanced sampling may undersample rare events and inadequately resolve finite-size effects.
Ultrasmall particles or very high temperatures may require refinement of the simulation model or additional methods.
Force-field accuracy and finite computational sampling limit quantitative estimates of the relationship between particle size and barrier height.
Failure to observe increasing barriers or stability with size would falsify the proposed size-stability trend.
